subject: Science
unit: Summer 1: Review of Key Stage 3 and working scientifically (9C)
source: Seeded from science/y9 lesson 44 (Hypothesis and variables worksheet with answers (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 44: Hypotheses, predictions and variables. To understand how a hypothesis leads to a testable prediction with clearly defined variables

model.title: Hypothesis: sugar dissolves faster in warm water because particles move faster.

parts.label: Step 3
parts.text: Prediction: if the temperature rises, then the dissolving time falls

parts.label: Answer
parts.text: If water temperature increases, the time for sugar to dissolve will decrease.

questions.q: Write a hypothesis for: 'Does exercise change heart rate?'
questions.a: Heart rate increases with exercise because muscles need more oxygen and glucose delivered
questions.model: Hypothesis = idea + reason. Idea: heart rate goes up. Reason: muscles respire more and need more oxygen. Join with 'because'.

questions.q: Name the independent variable in the exercise test.
Is 'type of fabric' categoric or continuous?
For four investigation questions on the sheet, write a hypothesis, the three types of variable and a prediction.
questions.a: Correct variables and testable predictions (as on the answer sheet)
questions.model: Teacher does question 1 on the board: 'Does the surface area of a tablet change how fast it dissolves?'

questions.q: Explain why a hypothesis can be supported but never fully proved.
questions.a: A new result could always disagree; more evidence only makes it more likely

questions.q: Suggest a control experiment for testing whether light is needed for photosynthesis.
questions.a: An identical plant kept in the dark (or a leaf covered with foil)

questions.q: The variable you change is the...
Big question: is 'plants grow towards light because they need it' a hypothesis?
questions.a: Yes: an explanation that can be tested by changing light and measuring growth.
